rows.title: Darkness or shadows in the room
rows.storyText:
Arin needs to cross a dark room to get something. Arin wanted to reach the other side and get the object, but the familiar room suddenly feels strange and scary in the darkness. The old thought came quickly: "Fear means I should stop." Arin could feel the familiar room suddenly seem strange and scary once the darkness started changing what each shape felt like. Arin first froze at the edge of the dark room, letting the strange-looking shadows decide what the whole room must mean. Arin wants to stop because the fear feels like a warning. 

Arin then kept feeding the scary feeling in their head, and because of that the same familiar room felt less and less familiar by the second. Arin was almost ready to let the darkness choose for them and turn one crossing into something much bigger than it really was. Arin paused anyway, let the room be the same room again for a moment, and chose one next step instead of answering every shadow at once. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "It's still the same room."
Arin then chose one small brave step into the dark room, because the way through was to cross the real room in front of them rather than obey the whole scary picture in their mind. 

Arin acted from the new understanding that courage is taking one small brave step, instead of from the first alarm.


Arin could feel the room become more familiar again once the next step answered the darkness better than the fear had. 

Arin felt their body loosen and could finally breathe easier as the dark room stopped acting like a stranger.
rows.compressedStory: Arin needs to cross a dark room to get something. Arin wanted to reach the other side and get the object, but the old thought said Fear means I should stop. After a quiet "Wait," Arin chose to look again and understood that Courage is taking one small brave step. Arin chose a different next step, and the problem eased into a warmer, freer ending.

rows.title: Monsters under the bed
rows.storyText:
Arin sees a shadow under the bed and imagines a monster hiding there. Arin wanted to find out whether the monster is real and feel safe enough to sleep, but arin's imagination keeps turning ordinary shadows into frightening shapes. The old thought came quickly: "My imagination can control me." Arin could feel one shadow under the bed growing into something much bigger once imagination started filling in what could not actually be seen. Arin first stayed far from the bed, letting the hidden space underneath it decide what kind of danger must be waiting there. The more Arin imagines, the more real the fear feels. 

Arin then kept adding more fearful pictures in their head, and each new imagined detail made the shadow feel more real than the room around it. Arin was almost ready to let the imagined monster choose the whole night and take away the chance to find out what was actually there. Arin paused anyway, let the bed become just a bed again for one moment, and chose to face the shadow instead of the whole imagined creature at once. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "I haven't checked what it really is yet."
Arin then chose one small brave move toward the bed, because the only way to answer the fear was to meet the real shadow instead of feeding the invented monster. 

Arin acted from the new understanding that I can be braver than my fears, instead of from the first alarm.


Arin could feel the shadow shrink back into an ordinary shape once the brave look answered it better than imagination had. 

Arin felt sleep come closer once the under-bed fear lost its monster shape.
rows.compressedStory: Arin's imagination keeps turning ordinary shadows into frightening shapes, and Arin believed My imagination can control me. Arin paused, chose to look again, and understood that I can be braver than my fears. Arin chose a different response, and the ending felt warmer and freer than before. The change was clear in what happened next.

rows.title: Injections at the doctor
rows.storyText:
Arin is at the doctor's office and knows an injection is coming. Arin wanted to avoid the injection or make it hurt less, but the appointment cannot simply be skipped. The old thought came quickly: "If something hurts, I can't handle it." 

Arin could feel the doctor visit narrowing around the coming injection, because the moment of pain had not happened yet but was already taking up too much space. Arin first tried to escape the injection in their mind, wishing the shot could somehow be skipped before it even began. Arin is afraid of pain that hasn't even happened yet.
Arin then tightened against the coming pinch, but bracing early only made the waiting chair feel longer and sharper. Arin was almost ready to let the expected pain decide the whole appointment before the shot had even happened. Arin paused anyway, listened for what was happening in the room right now, and chose to meet only the next small part of the doctor visit. 

"Wait," Arin told themselves. "I only have to get through the shot, not the whole future."


Arin then stayed present for the shot one brave beat at a time, because handling the real pinch was smaller than fighting the whole imagined appointment at once. Arin acted from the new understanding that I am stronger than I think, even during difficult moments, instead of from the first alarm.


Arin could feel the injection moment pass more cleanly once the fear stopped stretching it bigger than it was. 

Arin felt the doctor's room loosen around them once the waiting fear finally let go.

Arin paused, chose to look again, and understood that I am stronger than I think, even during difficult moments. Arin chose a different response, and the ending felt warmer and freer than before. The change was clear in what happened next.

rows.title: Fear of dogs
rows.storyText:
Arin is walking outside when a dog approaches. Arin wanted to stay safe without panicking, but the dog is unfamiliar and Arin is afraid of what it might do. The old thought came quickly: "Fear means I should avoid everything unfamiliar." Arin could feel that every second spent feeding the fear made the next step seem bigger. Arin first reacted the fast way, tightening up and bracing as if stopping completely might somehow make the fear go away. Fear says, Run! 

even though running may not be the safest choice. Arin then tried to rush the decision in their head, but the fear only spread into more corners of the moment. Arin was almost ready to let the fear make the choice for them, because the last safe-feeling chance seemed to be slipping away. Arin paused anyway, took one steadier breath, and let the next move become small enough to choose on purpose. "Wait," Arin told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well.
Arin then chose one small brave step instead of one panicked one, because responding to the real moment was safer than obeying the whole fear at once. 

Arin acted from the new understanding that I can learn, stay safe and become braver step by step, instead of from the first alarm.


Arin could feel that the brave step worked because the pause had helped them answer the real dog or dark moment in front of them, not the imagined one. 

Arin smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

rows.title: Their clothes aren't as 'cool' as others'
rows.storyText:
Gauri notices that classmates are wearing clothes or shoes that seem more fashionable than theirs. Gauri wanted to feel accepted without feeling different, but gauri cannot suddenly have everything the other children have. The old thought came quickly: "I need nicer things to be accepted." 

Gauri could feel the margin shrinking around the problem. Gauri first reacted quickly, hoping speed alone would solve it. Gauri begins believing that having nicer things would make them more liked. 

Gauri then pushed again, but the pressure only grew. Gauri was almost ready to let urgency make the final choice. Gauri paused anyway and chose one steadier beat before acting. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then made the final move with more care than panic. Gauri acted from the new understanding that who I am matters more than what I own, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri could feel that the pause had changed the final move for the better. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

rows.title: At a party but wanting the birthday gifts
rows.storyText:
Gauri watches a friend open one exciting birthday present after another and begins wishing the gifts were theirs. Gauri wanted to have the same exciting presents, but the presents belong to the birthday child. The old thought came quickly: "I'll only be happy if I get what someone else has." 

Gauri could feel each new cheer at the party making the wanting louder, because every package seemed to ask whose joy this was allowed to be. Gauri first imagined what it would feel like if the next bright package had their own name on it instead. Gauri wants to be happy for the friend while feeling increasingly disappointed about what they don't have. 

Gauri then cheered with everyone else while still comparing each present to what they did not have, and the party started feeling more like a fairness test than a celebration. Gauri was almost ready to let the wanting pull them all the way out of the birthday child's moment. Gauri paused before the next present opened and made room for one true thing that was still good at the party even without owning the gifts. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then chose to join the celebration as it really was, so they could stay inside the joy of the party without needing the present to belong to them. Gauri acted from the new understanding that celebrating others can bring joy too, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri got to stay inside the party's happiness once wanting stopped trying to turn every gift into a test of fairness. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

The old thought came quickly: "Having more things or popularity makes someone better." 

Gauri could feel one number on the screen trying to explain too much about who mattered. Gauri first stared at the two follower counts again, as if the gap itself might tell the whole truth about friendship and value. A number on a screen begins to feel like a measure of how much people value Gauri. 

Gauri then felt the comparison tighten further, because the friend's bigger number kept trying to turn into a verdict about gauri. Gauri was almost ready to let the number decide the whole mood of the moment and make the friendship feel smaller than it really was. Gauri paused, stopped refreshing the count, and looked for one truer sign of being cared for that existed off the screen too. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then chose to step back from the number and stay with the real friendship in front of them, because a count could not measure the whole of being valued. Gauri acted from the new understanding that real happiness and friendship can't be measured by possessions or popularity, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri felt lighter once the follower count stopped being treated like the final answer about how much people valued them. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

Gauri could feel the friend's exciting stories making ordinary parts of their own life suddenly seem too small. Gauri first followed every photograph and souvenir so closely that their own holiday began shrinking in comparison. The friend's stories make ordinary parts of Gauri's own life suddenly feel dull. 

Gauri then kept measuring their own life against the huge buildings, snow, and faraway places, and the comparison made ordinary memories feel duller than they had felt before. Gauri was almost ready to believe someone else's adventure had to reduce the worth of their own in order to count as special. Gauri paused on the envy, let the friend's stories stay exciting, and made room to remember that two different holidays could both matter. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then chose to stay in the conversation without demanding that their own life match it, because one person's excitement did not have to erase another's. Gauri acted from the new understanding that meaningful memories can be created anywhere, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri left the conversation steadier, able to hold the friend's joy and their own different life in the same moment. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

Gauri first looked back and forth between the two lunchboxes, letting the comparison change how their own food looked. Gauri suddenly feels dissatisfied with the lunch they were perfectly happy to eat a few minutes earlier. 

Gauri then kept chasing the smell and the picture of the other meal, and because of that their own next bite already felt less appealing than it had before. Gauri was almost ready to lose the whole lunch to comparison, even though the food they actually had was still right there. Gauri paused, stopped chasing the smell from the next seat, and returned attention to the lunch already open in front of them. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then chose the next bite from their own lunch on purpose, so the meal in front of them could become their real meal again. Gauri acted from the new understanding that gratitude helps me enjoy what I already have, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri got their lunch back by stopping the comparison, and the meal felt lighter again once it was allowed to be their own. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

Gauri could feel the pile of good options starting to crowd the decision instead of helping it. Gauri first tried to keep every toy or treat equally alive in their mind, afraid that choosing one would mean losing all the others. The more Gauri compares the choices, the more afraid they become of choosing the wrong one. 

Gauri then compared the options again and again, but more comparing only made the best choice feel harder to see. Gauri was almost ready to let the number of choices ruin the chance to enjoy any choice at all. Gauri paused, stopped trying to keep every option open, and looked for the one choice that actually fit this moment best. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves. "One good choice is enough." Gauri then chose one toy or treat on purpose, because a wise choice could bring more peace than trying to hold on to everything. 

Gauri acted from the new understanding that wise choices matter more than having everything, instead of from the first alarm. Gauri felt the decision settle once one real choice replaced the scramble to keep every possibility. Gauri smiled once the choice finally belonged to this moment instead of all the others.

rows.title: Family having to cut back on treats or outings
rows.storyText:
Gauri asks for a usual treat or outing and learns that the family needs to spend less money for a while. Gauri wanted to have the familiar treat or outing anyway, but the family has a temporary financial limit. The old thought came quickly: "Happiness comes from having more." 

Gauri could feel one small "no" growing heavy because the usual treat had started to stand for something bigger about the family. Gauri first held on to the usual Friday treat itself, because losing that familiar yes felt like losing the whole shape of the day. Gauri feels the disappointment of a small 'no' without fully understanding the bigger reason behind it. 

Gauri then pushed against the change inside, but the disappointment only grew sharper because the family limit still stayed real. Gauri was almost ready to let that one missing treat decide that the whole moment was unfair, even though the bigger reason had already been gently named. Gauri paused, stopped arguing with the missing treat, and listened again to the careful-for-now reason underneath the answer. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves, before spending the last bit of courage well. Gauri then chose to accept the changed family plan and stay with the people in front of them, because a temporary limit did not mean love had disappeared. Gauri acted from the new understanding that love, togetherness and gratitude bring lasting happiness, instead of from the first alarm. 

Gauri understood the family's temporary limit more gently once the missing treat stopped being used as proof that something deeper was wrong. Gauri smiled and could feel the ending settle more calmly now.

rows.title: Watched someone get bullied and did nothing

Arin sees another child being teased or treated cruelly and does not know whether or how to step in. Arin wanted to make the situation stop or help the child, but arin feels unsure, afraid, or too small to handle the situation alone. The old thought came quickly: "Speaking up won't make a difference." 

Arin could feel the moment closing fast, because the teasing was happening now and silence would become its own choice very soon. Arin first stayed still, hoping the cruel moment might end on its own before they had to decide anything. Arin wants to help but worries about becoming the next target. 

Arin then rushed through fearful possibilities in their head, but each silent second made the need to protect the other child feel sharper.
Arin was almost ready to let fear make the final choice and leave the other child alone inside the teasing. Arin paused, stopped rehearsing every worst outcome, and made room for one small brave action that could protect someone right now. 

"Wait," Arin told themselves. "Someone needs help now." Arin then chose the smallest real step that interrupted the cruelty, because a brave action in time mattered more than a perfect plan too late. 

Arin acted from the new understanding that small acts of courage can protect others, instead of from the first alarm. Arin could feel the moment change once courage turned into protection instead of staying trapped inside worry. Arin could feel relief arrive with the courage instead of after it.

Gauri wanted to share in the excitement without feeling jealous, but the pet belongs to the friend, and Gauri cannot simply have one too. The old thought came quickly: "Life is unfair because I don't have what they have." 

Gauri could feel the friend's good news pulling jealousy close, because the wished-for pet made the gap between lives feel personal. Gauri first stayed fixed on the pet itself, measuring what the friend had against what they still wished for. Gauri genuinely loves the animal but finds it difficult to separate happiness for the friend from the wish that it were theirs. 

Gauri then let the comparison keep growing, and the more the dream pet filled the moment, the harder it became to share the friend's excitement honestly. Gauri was almost ready to let the missing pet decide that the friendship's happy moment could not also hold their own goodness. Gauri paused, noticed the jealousy without obeying it, and made room for one true thing in their own life that still deserved appreciation too. 

"Wait," Gauri told themselves. "Their joy is not taking mine away." Gauri then chose to share in the friend's excitement anyway, because someone else's joy did not have to cancel their own life. 

Gauri acted from the new understanding that I can be genuinely happy for others while appreciating my own life, instead of from the first alarm. Gauri felt the envy loosen once the friend's new pet stopped being treated like proof that life was unfair. Gauri smiled when the friendship finally felt bigger than the comparison again.
